summary: I attacked this hard and the architecture held. Its central new claim — that /goal exists natively in both Codex and Claude Code, so no custom runtime need emulate a persisted goal — I verified independently: the installed claude 2.1.222 binary contains /goal, '/goal active', '/goal clear to stop early', '/goal <condition> to set another', plus getStopHookMessage, executeStopHooks, stopHookActive and stopHookBlockingCount beside turnCount/maxTurns, confirming the condition-based Stop-hook implementation; and ~/.codex/goals_1.sqlite ships thread_goals with objective, six statuses and token_budget/tokens_used/time_used_seconds. The derived design is sharper than generic: recognizing that Codex self-audits completion while Claude's evaluator is blind to the filesystem, and therefore that one STATUS block serves as completion condition on one route and premature-idle detector on the other, with a mandatory turn bound for Claude, is a real insight. Using sqlite3 on the goal store in the recovery script is the best answer to Q2 in either document. The Paseo read-asymmetry finding (only logs without --tail is unfragmented; wait/send/foreground run all look like results and are not) is exactly what a spec exists to name, and the previously dangling section-21 sources reference is gone. Remaining defects are narrow amendments, not redesigns: it misses two verified hard preconditions on Claude /goal — 'only available in trusted workspaces' and 'allowManagedHooksOnly' — and the trust gate contradicts its own section 5.3, which launches the executor into a brand-new worktree path via paseo run --new-workspace worktree; moving helpers into mo-orchestrate/scripts/ (a correct packaging fix) strands mo-lastmsg away from standalone mo-review, its own headline use case advertised via npx skills add --skill mo-review; its [V] marker now conflates 'ran here' with 'read upstream source', and for the uninstalled Paseo it dropped last round's explicit unvalidated assumption and risk row; refs/mo/candidate is still an unnamespaced global ref; interrogate at fail-under=100 with all ignores false still risks ritual docstrings with only file-level escapes; and making the STATUS block the literal goal condition creates a cheapest-path incentive that must be labeled a handoff signal rather than gate evidence.

blocking_findings.area: Claude /goal preconditions and the worktree contradiction
blocking_findings.description: The installed claude 2.1.222 binary contains two hard gates the proposal does not state: '/goal is only available in trusted workspaces. Restart, accept the trust dialog, and try again.' and '/goal can't run while hooks are restricted (disableAllHooks or allowManagedHooksOnly is set in settings or by policy).' Only disableAllHooks is mentioned; trust is absent entirely. The trust gate collides with section 5.3 S2, which launches the executor as 'paseo run -d --new-workspace worktree --worktree-mode branch-off', placing it in a brand-new directory path — untrusted until a dialog is accepted, silently disabling /goal on the Claude route, and the dialog is itself an interactive prompt that --dangerously-skip-permissions is not documented to bypass. This directly contradicts section 16.3, which confines worktrees to gates. Both failures are silent: /goal degrades to the weaker fallback without announcing it, which is the exact hazard the task's 'do not pass a fallback off as equivalent' clause targets.
blocking_findings.required_change: Extend preflight from command -v to a triple: PATH resolution, workspace trust for any directory a /goal-bearing role will run in, and hook policy (disableAllHooks and allowManagedHooksOnly). State explicitly that a /goal-bearing executor must not be launched into a freshly created worktree path unless trust is pre-established, resolving section 5.3 in favour of section 16.3.

blocking_findings.area: evidence-marker conflation for the uninstalled backend
blocking_findings.description: [V] is defined to cover both execution on this machine and reading upstream source. For the installed tools this is harmless and I verified many such claims without error. For Paseo — not installed — every claim is a read of upstream HEAD, and constants such as CODEX_GOALS_MIN_VERSION = [0,128,0], DEFAULT_MAX_ITEMS = 0, WAIT_ACTIVITY_PREVIEW_COUNT = 5 and DEFAULT_FOLLOW_TAIL = 10 are precisely what drifts between HEAD and a released version. This is a regression from the previous revision, which carried an explicit '[A] Paseo unvalidated' assumption and a Paseo-incompatibility risk row; both are now absent, so the tables no longer signal which Paseo facts are unproven locally, even though Phase 0 still installs it.
blocking_findings.required_change: Split the marker into runtime-verified and source-read (or adopt Proposal 1's available/inferred/unavailable/fallback vocabulary), mark every Paseo capability as source-read/inferred until Phase 0, and restore the Paseo-incompatibility risk row and the unvalidated-until-installed assumption.

blocking_findings.description: Placing mo-models.mjs and mo-lastmsg.mjs inside mo-orchestrate/scripts/ is correct reasoning about how apm and npx skills copy whole skill directories. But standalone mo-review is a headline requirement and the proposal explicitly advertises installing it alone via 'npx skills add --skill mo-review'. On Herdr a standalone review needs the full reviewer verdict, whose only non-obedience-dependent path is mo-lastmsg — which that installation does not include. The most-advertised standalone use case therefore loses its fallback retrieval path exactly where Herdr has no native full-message API.
blocking_findings.required_change: Place mo-lastmsg.mjs in mo-review/scripts/ (its consumer for the standalone case), duplicating the ~80 read-only lines into mo-orchestrate/scripts/ if needed; a duplicated copy is cheaper than a cross-skill runtime dependency and matches the document's own reasoning about copying shared references.

blocking_findings.description: For Claude the goal condition is that the transcript contains a STATUS block with SCOPE-COMPLETE: yes, TESTS: pass, QC: pass and a clean commit sha. Since the evaluator cannot read files or run commands, the cheapest way to satisfy the goal is to print the block, and the evaluator cannot distinguish a truthful from a fabricated one. Downstream re-checks cover the falsifiable fields (the orchestrator re-runs make mo-qc on the candidate; sha and git status --porcelain are checkable), leaving SCOPE-COMPLETE judged only by reviewers — acceptable, but the document does not say that the block is not evidence.
blocking_findings.required_change: State explicitly that the STATUS block is a handoff/liveness signal and never gate evidence, and that the orchestrator must independently re-derive QC result, commit cleanliness and sha rather than trusting the block's claims.

blocking_findings.area: candidate ref namespacing and purpose-coverage noise
blocking_findings.description: refs/mo/candidate remains a single unnamespaced global ref — the one fact persisted outside sessions. Two features in flight in one repository (plausible under the self-hosting scenario the task contemplates) collide silently, and a ref left from a finished feature is reported by the section 4.2 no-argument flow as unfinished work; the risk table still covers only accidental deletion. Separately, interrogate fail-under=100 with ignore-private, ignore-magic, ignore-nested-functions, ignore-nested-classes and ignore-semiprivate all false demands a docstring on every closure and dunder, with only a file-level exclusion list, risking the 'бессмысленные повторяющиеся docstrings' the task warns against despite the sound coverage/depth split.
blocking_findings.required_change: Namespace the ref as refs/mo/candidate/<branch-slug>, delete it on completion, and state that a stale ref is reconciled against git log rather than trusted. Add a documented symbol-class allowance (trivial accessors, short closures) alongside the file-level exclusions.

assumptions: String extraction from the installed Claude Code 2.1.222 binary is sound evidence for the existence, wording and preconditions of /goal; I did not execute /goal end to end.

thread_goals in ~/.codex/goals_1.sqlite currently has zero rows, so goal mode has never run on this machine; the shipped migration proves the capability but end-to-end behaviour still needs the Phase 0 live test the proposal already schedules.

Paseo source-level claims (min version gate, DEFAULT_MAX_ITEMS, preview/follow-tail constants, findExecutable) are accurate for upstream HEAD but unverified against any installed release; I could not check them offline.

Oxlint, node:test and eslint-config-prettier claims I could not verify offline are accurate as stated; they support conservative conclusions, so an error would not change the recommended default profile.
